issues.problem: The card says 'Every row below mirrors reports/friday_v7/plays.json, which is the reconciled source of truth for this week' and prints 38 plays - but SEVEN SHADOW dispositions from the body never became plays. Missing: (1) the abs_veto_short exit ladder 1.5R/2.5R -> 1.0R/1.5R, which Part 2 SS10 itself labels 'The week's main proposal'; (2) exhaustion_short tight-chandelier on the trend rungs (Part 2 SS8d, already written to data/exit_overrides_proposed.json); (3) grind_long MED-TREND A0.5/B1.0; (4) the two short faders as run-catchers (M2); (5) capitulation_long 'require_flip OR 90-second timeout' (M2); (6) the quiet-tape-clip range-break suspension (M2, second consecutive week at ~$1,000); (7) exhaustion_short's 'the flow DID move price' clause inverted as a bench instrument (M2). I grepped plays.json - none of the 38 rows is any of these. Under the scope's own doctrine SHADOW is free and is the default disposition, so a SHADOW verdict that produces no play is a lost week of incubation.
issues.fix: Add the seven as SHADOW/BUILD rows (shadow slates cost nothing and need no Saturday deploy), or add one line under each disposition saying why a SHADOW verdict deliberately carries no action. At minimum promote Part 2's self-declared main proposal onto the card.

issues.problem: Direct contradiction on the same gate's profit ladder, and neither section cites the other. Part 1 SS2.2 - the report's self-declared best-evidenced result - shows abs_veto_short's WIDE leg (2.5R) beat its TIGHT leg (1.5R) by +$65.00 over 12 paired signals, and MONDAY #1 turns that into a desk-wide instruction to widen Lot A's target. Part 2 SS3 then diagnoses the very same gate's 1.5R/2.5R ladder as TOO WIDE ('it converts winners into stop-outs') and proposes bringing it IN to 1.0R/1.5R. Follow the card and Garrath widens A on abs_veto_short on Monday while the shadow section wants it tightened.
issues.fix: Reconcile explicitly. The paired within-gate test (n=12) and the live-vs-shadow exit-mix diagnosis point opposite ways on abs_veto_short - state which governs, and scope MONDAY #1 to the gates the paired evidence actually supports (exhaustion_short carries +$225.50 of the +$331.50; abs_veto_short carries $65 on 12 pairs).

issues.problem: Two separate rehabs land on two different exits for exhaustion_short and the report never picks one. Part 1.5 concludes the fix is a 1.5xATR stop with a far target and a 15-minute cap (+$3,459.98 vs -$84.50) and BUILD #1 shadow-slates that. Part 2 SS8d concludes the fix is a TIGHT CHANDELIER on both lots for BIG-TREND and MED-TREND (+$22.8 and +$8.3 a signal on a plateau) and writes it to data/exit_overrides_proposed.json as the deliverable. These are different exit families for the same gate on overlapping populations. Part 1.5 SS8 mentions Part 2 only as a caution about the live fade-scalp trial; it never mentions SS8d's competing proposal, and only one of the two is on the card.
issues.fix: Run them head-to-head on the same 87 tape-backed signals split by rung, and put ONE proposal in the shadow book - or state plainly that the wide-stop policy is the chop/all-regime answer and the tight chandelier is the trend-rung answer, with the rung boundary named.

issues.section: Part 2.5 Part C vs Part 2.6 SS3 vs SATURDAY #3
issues.problem: The selector phantom is priced two incompatible ways in the same report. Part 2.5 Part C: regret $748 -> $458, 'inflated 39%', i.e. $290 of phantom. Part 2.6 SS3: '$362.50, or 48% of the day's entire regret' and 'read Thursday's selector row as roughly $385 of regret on 9 real trades'. I checked data/selector_nightly/2026-08-13.json: there are exactly five identical day_rider rows at $72.50 regret each, and only FOUR of the underlying trade rows are quarantined (ids 673/674/675/678) - the 13:38 LONG that Garrath claimed at 14:26 for +$731 is real. So $290 / $458 / 10 trades is right and Part 2.6's restatement deletes the real trade too. Part 2.5 also states both 39% and 48% within its own section. SATURDAY #3's verification criterion is 'confirm regret drops from $748 to $458' - which will FAIL if whoever fixes it follows Part 2.6.
issues.fix: Use $290 phantom / $458 corrected / 10 real trades everywhere, and drop the 48% figure (it counts the genuine rider trade as phantom). Then the SATURDAY #3 verification stands.

issues.problem: The report counts the router's own switch changes two ways and never reconciles them. Part 1 says '60 switch changes... 67 individual gate keys' with per-day 9/20/16/11/4 and 28 arm events. Part 2.6 SS1 does the three-way reconciliation the desk's own standing lesson demands (router log under-reports, systemd journal over-reports, gate_switches.env mtime is the arbiter) and lands on 56 TRUE switch events / 64 gate transitions for Tue-Fri - which is 73 gate flips once Monday's 9 are added - with the router-log column reading Tue 21 and Thu 12 against Part 1's 20 and 11, and 31 arms against Part 1's 28. Part 1 is quoting the instrument Part 2.6 proves is wrong.
issues.fix: Restate Part 1 SS6.1/SS8 off the reconciled gate_switches.env counts, or label them 'router log only, see Part 2.6 SS1 for the reconciliation' and carry the same arm-event count in both places.

issues.problem: The front scorecard says the router ran '1,148 ticks, zero service failures, 95% of ticks change nothing'. Part 1 SS6.1's table says 1,440 total ticks with 1,210 genuine no-change (84%) and 125 ABORTs. 1,148 is Tue-Fri only (288x3 + 284) and is presented on the front page as the week. 'Zero service failures' is also literally true only of systemd - the same row then reports 125 consecutive aborted decisions - which reads as self-contradiction on the one page most people will actually read.
issues.fix: On the front: '1,148 ticks Tue-Fri (Monday unverifiable - journal retention), zero systemd failures, 125 aborted decisions on 08-13, 95% of ticks change nothing.' Make the Part 1 table use the same window or say why it doesn't.

issues.problem: The census's own closing sentence contradicts its own table. It says 'The runs made money and the fading gave it back' and the intro says 'The bleed is not the runs; it is the fading we do around them' - but the HONEST MONEY table shows Fought (against) = 5 runs, +$92, and two of the five fought rows are +$82 (08-10 13:35) and +$170 (08-14 13:37). On this week's census, fading around the runs MADE money. The 'bleed' framing is inherited, not computed.
issues.fix: Rewrite both sentences to what the table says: the fading was roughly a wash-to-positive on the runs themselves (+$92 on 5); the money on the table is the 60 sat-out runs and the $8,024 ceiling, which is a not-showing-up problem, not a fading problem.

issues.problem: The gold census is the MNQ template with the numbers swapped and the prose left untouched, and it produces nonsense. 'We caught 0, we were positioned against 0, and we sat out 74. The runs we aligned with banked +$0 of honest money - but that is only 0% of their $0 hindsight ceiling' - and then, on an instrument the desk has never placed a trade in, 'The runs made money and the fading gave it back; we convert a fraction of the ceiling and ignore the rest.' There is no fading to give anything back.
issues.fix: Write gold its own two paragraphs: no MNQ gate is even eligible on MGC, so 100% of the $10,649 single-lot ceiling is on the table by construction, and the honest question is which of the 74 runs the Part 2.5 gold candidates (day rider, coil bouncer) would have been in. That turns a template artefact into the census's actual finding.

issues.problem: The gold census has no order-book read at all - the 'book' column is em-dash on all 74 rows - even though the column header explains what it means, the scope requires a per-run L2 book read, and the data contract says MGC depth lives in depth.db.depth_snap (capture.db.book is MNQ-only). Movement 3's entire gold hunt is a 397-break order-book study on the same instrument, so the depth data plainly exists and is queryable.
issues.fix: Populate the MGC book column from depth.db.depth_snap (250ms sample), or state in the census header that the 250ms sample cannot resolve a 15-minute run's ignition and point at Movement 3 for what the book does say about gold - which is that far-side depletion is inverted.

issues.problem: The section written specifically to expose a baseline error repeats it in its own table. It correctly re-baselines to the deployed net_min 400 (n=70, +$556.50) - but the 'cut' and 'winners forgone' columns are still measured from the UNFILTERED 87. Verified in exh_netmin.json: net_min 450 has cut_n=30 and forgone_winner_usd=640.0, which is 87-57, not 70-57. Against the live floor, 450 cuts 13 more signals and forgoes $476.50 of winners, not 30 and $640. The closing line - 'by net_min 900 the floor has thrown away $2,761 of winning signals to dodge $2,858 of losing ones' - is likewise the no-floor figure (json: forgone 2761.0 / avoided 2858.5 on cut_n=83), not the incremental one. The verdict (every higher floor is worse) is unaffected; the numbers quoted for it are the wrong baseline.
issues.fix: Add incremental columns measured from the 70-signal live-400 baseline, and restate the closing sentence with the incremental pair. It is a two-line change and it is the difference between the section demonstrating the lesson and repeating the mistake.

issues.problem: The load-bearing random-entry control does not tie to the headline number. SS7's headline cell is 1.5xATR stop / 3.0xATR target = $3,459.98, quoted in SS8, SS9, the front scorecard and BUILD #1. SS7.2's control table calls the same policy 'stop 1.5xATR / target 2.0R / 15min cap', reports the same exit mix (22 target / 31 stop / 34 time), and scores it $3,465.48 - from which the entry alpha of $3,467.78 is derived. Same policy, two labels (ATR vs R), two totals $5.50 apart, and the alpha that the whole rehabilitation rests on is computed off the one that is never shown anywhere else.
issues.fix: Use one unit and one number. If the control run genuinely differs (different cap handling, different tie-break on the stop-before-target check), say so in a footnote and quote both.

issues.section: MONDAY #2 (Open Rider stop width) vs Part 2 SS5

Part 2 SS5 closes the stop-width axis with 'Every Open Rider arm is flagged n < 40, below this desk's threshold for a forward A/B to claim anything. No promotion follows from this week, on any cell, in either direction' - and shows the DAY effect is 2.2x the stop effect. The card nonetheless puts 'Open Rider: stop at 3.0xATR, not 2.0x' in the MONDAY at-the-desk window, mode 'config', owner 'day rider config' - i.e. a live change to the desk's only profitable engine, which went 5-for-5 this week under its current settings.

issues.problem: The report discredits a figure and then quotes the discredited figure three times. Leg 2 shows abs_veto_robustness.py's per-day leg does not reconcile (it drops all four Sunday sessions, has 07-28 at 28 trades where the ledger has 33), recomputes it from shadow.db as 18 of 25 days green, and instructs 'Use these; the script's per-day leg needs a fix'. The one-paragraph version, the SS10 disposition and HOLD play #4 then all cite '16 of 21 days green' - the script's number.

issues.problem: The census's 'real $' column looks like a single-lot number, which breaks the ceiling-vs-honest-money reconciliation the scope requires. Every one of the eight caught/fought rows names an '_A' leg only. Concretely: the 08-12 13:50 DN run is scored at -$8 against exhaustion_short_A, while Part 1 SS5.2 books that same gate entering at 13:50:11 at 29,956.00 for +$123.00 across both lots ('Target + chandelier'). So the headline 'caught 3 -> +$237 of a $470 ceiling = 50% conversion' and 'fought 5 -> +$92' are half-book figures that do not tie to Part 1's per-signal money.
issues.fix: Sum both lots per signal in the real$ column (the scope asks for the reconciliation against the actual gate), or rename the column 'Lot A real $' and add the both-lot total beside it so the conversion percentage means what it says.

unanswered.question: The single biggest bucket of loss this week is $1,058 of trades that were up a median 39 points and travelled all the way to a full stop. Part 1 SS11 names the fix it has NOT tested - bank one lot of the two at a fixed points-onside and let the other run - calls it 'the first thing I would test next week', and then it never appears on the plays card at all. So the report's own largest diagnosed loss has no action against it.
unanswered.how_to_answer: Replay the 33 losing signals AND the 25 winning ones (the SS9.2 apply-to-all-lots honesty test) with Lot A banking at +8/+10/+12/+15/+20pt onside on the 5-second bars, favourable move required in a strictly earlier bar than the exit bar, Lot B unchanged on its existing exit. Report net, the winners-kept count, LODO and a placebo, and put the surviving cell on next week's card. The scale-out already gives two lots, so it costs nothing structurally.

unanswered.question: Which exhaustion_short exit actually goes into the shadow book on Monday - the 1.5xATR stop with a far target (BUILD #1) or the tight chandelier on both lots (Part 2 SS8d, already written to exit_overrides_proposed.json)? Two studies in the same report reached two different answers on the same gate and neither is graded against the other.
unanswered.how_to_answer: Reprice both policies on the identical 87 tape-backed signals, split by the SS8b rung (BIG-TREND / MED-TREND / SCALP-CHOP), with the same random-entry control applied to each. If the chandelier wins the trend rungs and the wide stop wins overall, ship a rung-conditional shadow slate and say so; if they are within noise, ship the simpler one.

unanswered.question: Is the live-vs-shadow abs_veto_short gap ($2,349 over fifteen days) really the exit ladder, or is it fills? The diagnosis is inferred entirely from the exit-reason mix - same winner size, 33% bigger losers - and the report elsewhere states its own standing finding that live losses run 1.1-3.1x modelled. Nothing in the section measures actual slippage, so 'the ladder is too wide' and 'we get filled worse than the repricer assumes' produce the same table.
unanswered.how_to_answer: For each of the 63 live short legs, compare the actual fill price against the configured stop/target level and report the per-leg slippage distribution. Then re-run the shadow twin with that measured slippage applied. If the gap survives, it is the ladder; if it closes, the ladder change would be fixing the wrong thing and the forward A/B would prove nothing.

unanswered.question: The day rider produced $1,617.50 of the desk's $1,292.50 - take it out and the week is red - yet four of its five trades have no venue execution record and two are hand-reconstructed with an exit reason ('CLOCK_FLAT_RECON') that no code in the repo emits. The report says this plainly, but never asks the obvious follow-on: how much of the $1,617.50 would survive a venue-verified accounting, and what is the rider's actual edge as opposed to its booked one?
unanswered.how_to_answer: Score the five live trades against the 41-day deterministic replay the Open Rider section already built - same days, same clock - and report the live-minus-replay delta per day. Combine with the $263.50 of reconstructed P&L flagged separately. Then re-check next Friday that the fills-gap fix covers 5 of 5, not 1 of 5, before any number from this desk is quoted as proven.

unanswered.question: The Saturday #1 router timing change (+$502 / +$399) rests on 4 of 40 days, on a 40-day window the section itself calls 'overwhelmingly ONE regime' with this week at 84% chop - and the router is a trend instrument. The section flags this but does not test it. So: does 45/5/3 survive on the trending days specifically, or is it only ever measured where the router has nothing to do?
unanswered.how_to_answer: Rank the 40 days by session ER, hold out the top 8, and score the shipped config against 45/5/3 on those 8 alone. Also report which 4 days produced the +$502 and what their regime labels were. If all four are chop days, the change is being fitted on the regime it least matters in and the caveat needs to be a blocker, not a commit-message note.

unanswered.question: SATURDAY #2 - benching exhaustion_short against a proven counter-trend - is priced at n=26 / -$398.50 using the nightly's scalp-2R ruler, and Part 2.6 SS3 proves that same ruler is $7.26 a trade more generous than the desk and +$25.02 a trade more generous specifically in TREND_UP, which is exactly the regime the 26 fires sit in. The report uses the ruler to refuse the exhaustion_short over-bench figure and then uses it to justify the bench. Both cannot be right.
unanswered.how_to_answer: Reprice the 26 counter-trend fires under the LIVE two-lot exit as well as the nightly's scalp-2R and print both columns. The bench is still probably right - it is the cheap direction to be wrong in and it is red on 7 of 8 days - but the dollar figure on the card should be the one measured with the ruler the desk actually trades.

unanswered.question: The OPEN/NEWS cluster is 22 of this week's 68 runs and roughly $2,596 of the $8,024 ceiling, no gate on this desk has ever been built for it, and its hunt has now been scheduled and not run. What actually stops it running - and will BUILD #2 be enough, given the same budget exhaustion killed four hunts and truncated the rehab phase?
unanswered.how_to_answer: Beyond reordering the queue, state the phase budget arithmetic: the rehab phase took its full 90 minutes and the serial runner reported '0m left'. Either cap the rehab phase, or run the greenfield hunts first, or split them into their own run. A scheduling promise without the budget change is the same promise that failed this week.

unanswered.question: Part 2 SS6 says the two-ratchet watch books +$159 live on a grind trade whose maximum favourable excursion was 0.81R - about $23 a lot at ATR 14.1 - and calls that 'not physically reachable on the tape', pointing at the known fill mis-attribution mechanism. That is not a shadow-tool problem, it is a live-P&L integrity problem, and the report parks it as an instrument note.
unanswered.how_to_answer: Take every grind_long trade in the 26-trade window, compute each one's maximum favourable excursion from the tick tape, and flag every trade whose booked P&L exceeds its physical MFE. If more than the one trade fails, the live grind book is carrying mis-attributed fills and its all-time -$454.00 in the Part 2 SS4 table is not trustworthy either. That belongs on the card as a measurement gap, not in a footnote.
